t: Section 1833(g)(5) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395l(g)(5)) is amended by striking “and ending on” and all that follows through “2010” and inserting “and ending on December 31, 2011”.

fable.w: This section only amends a date range in Section 1833(g)(5) of the Social Security Act, extending an existing provision through December 31, 2011. A tempting reading is that the underlying provision involves a process engaging outside parties, but the text here is a purely technical date extension. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.

opus.w: This section is a technical amendment that only extends a deadline in the Social Security Act from 2010 to December 31, 2011. It provides for no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. One might think it brings in outsiders because the underlying provision covers a Medicare exceptions process, but nothing about that appears in this text, and asking for a benefit exception is like an application, which the definition excludes.
opus.s: is amended by striking “and ending on” and all that follows through “2010” and inserting “and ending on December 31, 2011”.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that changes a specific date in the Social Security Act. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, comment, or coordination with parties outside the federal government. The text contains no reference to public hearings, advisory committees, state consultation, or rights to sue.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1833(g)(5) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395l(g)(5)) is amended by striking “and ending on” and all that follows through “2010” and inserting “and ending on December 31, 2011”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the end date of a program affects public participation if the program involved public input, but the text itself is merely a technical amendment to a date. It does not establish, require, or describe any process for outside parties to consult with the government. The text is purely administrative and legislative housekeeping.
